chunks: He to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, who has neither begotten a son nor has He a partner in His kingdom, (who) created everything and determined its exact measure.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's ownership of the heavens and earth and His lack of partners?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Furqan is often cited to affirm Tawhid al-Dhat (Oneness of Essence) and Tawhid al-Sifat (Oneness of Attributes), refuting the Christian doctrine of divine sonship and polytheistic associations. The phrase 'created everything and determined it with precision' (Qaddarahu Taqdira) underscores God's deliberate and measured creation, a concept linked to the divine wisdom (Hikmah) that governs the cosmos. This precision reflects the Shia understanding of a purposeful universe where every entity has a designated role and measure, reinforcing the absolute sovereignty of Allah without any partners or offspring.
